description.narrative:
African Academy of Sciences (AAS) har hos Sida ansökt om 98,4 miljoner SEK för att genomföra programmet Grand Challenges (GC) Africa under perioden 2018-07-01 till 2023-06-30.
GC Africa är ett program som har målsättningen att stödja innovationer som ska bidra till att hitta lösningar för Afrikas utmaningar med att nå de Globala målen för hållbar utveckling. Det grundläggande konceptet bakom alla GC program är finansiering av innovativa idéer riktade mot specifika frågeställningar utan krav på preliminära resultat. GC Africa placerar konceptet i ett afrikanskt sammanhang och definierar frågeställningar/utmaningar relevanta i den afrikanska kontexten och programmet riktar sig specifikt mot afrikanska forskare verksamma vid universitet och organisationer baserade på den afrikanska kontinenten.
Programmet GC Africa har sin bas på Alliance for Accelerating Excellence in Science in Africa (AESA), ett programinitiativ grundat av AAS och organisationen New Partnership for Africa’s Development med syftet att tackla Afrikas utmaningar inom hälsa och utveckling. AESA har etablerat och driver olika program för att stödja forskare och forskning i Africa samt utveckla akademisk ledarskap och initiativ till innovationer. Sidas avtalspartner kommer att vara AAS, en ny partnerorganisation för Sida.
Den planerade totala budgeten för GC Africa programmet är ca. 246,5 miljoner SEK (28 miljoner USD) varav ca 86,5 miljoner SEK (9,85 miljoner USD) är finansierade av Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, Institute Pasteur och South African Medical Research Council. AAS har en pågående satsning att hitta fler givare till programmet, bland annat ska afrikanska regeringar och filantroper förmås att bidra. Av Sidas stöd till GC Africa kommer ca. 65,4 miljoner SEK att vidareförmedlas till forskningsprojekt.

The African Academy of Sciences (AAS) has applied to Sida for funding of 98,4 million SEK to contribute to the Grand Challenges (GC) Africa program during the period 2018-07-01 until 2013-06-30.
The GC Africa program aims at supporting the creation of innovations targeting developmental challenges preventing African countries from attaining the Global Goals for Sustainable Development. The basic concept of all GC programs includes grant support to research projects responding to pre-defined challenges not requiring extensive preliminary data. GC Africa has adapted this concept to the African context and established a program open to African researcher based at African universities and institutions and addresses challenges specific to African development needs.
GC Africa is a program of the Alliance for Accelerating Science in Africa (AESA) that is a programmatic platform founded by the AAS and the organization New Partnership for Africa's Development with the aim to address Africa's health and development challenges. AESA has established and drives different programs to support researchers and research projects in Africa and to develop academic leadership and innovations. Sida will enter into agreement with the AAS, a new partner organization for Sida.
The envisaged total budget of the GC Africa program is approximately 246,5 million SEK (28 million USD), out of which 86,5 million SEK (9,85 million USD) have been contributed by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, Institute Pasteur and the South African Medical Research Council. The AAS is in the process of attracting additional funders to the program and is approaching African governments and philanthropists. Of Sida’s support to the GC Africa program approximately 65,4 million SEK will be forwarded to research projects.

The overall objective of the intervention is to promote Africa-led scientific innovations to help countries better achieve the Sustainable Development Goals by awarding seed and full grants to the continent’s most impressive solutions.

In July 2018, Sida entered into a 5-year agreement with the African Academy of Science (AAS) regarding support to the GC Africa programme. At the AAS, the programme was implemented by the programmatic platform Alliance for Accelerating Excellence in Science in Africa (AESA).
The GC Africa programme applied a 2-stage approach supporting Africa-led scientific innovations at proof-of-concept and transition-to-scale stages. At the proof-of-concept stage, projects could apply for seed capital to make early, real-world assessments of technical, organisational and financial viability by piloting an innovation in the context of low- and middle-income countries. At the transition-to-scale stage, projects could apply for catalytic capital to facilitate business model development and support innovations that have demonstrated success at small scale.
The first GC Africa call in partnership with Sida was announced in September 2018. The proof-of-concept call Innovation for WASH (water, sanitation and hygiene) in urban settings was part of a global GC call initiative in partnership with Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF) and UNICEF and designed to respond to on-the-ground needs of women, children, and families living in challenging urban environments. The call received a good response from African scientists and research institutions (166 submitted grant proposals) and seven projects were selected for funding.
A major milestone for the programme was the announcement of the first round of GC Africa transition-to-scale grants in 2019. In this call, GC Africa invited African innovators that had received proof-of-concept grants in previous calls financed by partners in the GC family, including GC Explorations by BMGF, GC Canada, USAID Centre for Development Innovation, GC South Africa and GC Africa, to submit proposals for transition-to-scale support. The call received 106 applications of which 55 went into a review and curation process. After evaluation by an independent panel of scientific and business experts, nine innovative projects were selected for grant support by Sida, BMGF, GC Canada and South Africa Medical Research Council. The call was followed by a second transition-to-scale call in 2020 that resulted in the funding of 13 projects by Sida and BMGF.
In 2020, the GC Africa team quickly responded to the COVID-19 pandemic by organising webinars and surveys to define urgent COVID-19 research priorities for Africa. These exercises resulted in the publication of the policy paper Research and development priorities for COVID-19 in Africa that provided the basis for the research and innovation call Funding for COVID-19 research & development goals for Africa. The call resulted in 13 projects supported by Sida, BMGF and Wellcome Trust.
The GC Africa programme also published the policy paper Setting scientific priorities for food security and nutrition in Africa and announced the call Promoting innovations to advance food security and nutrition in Africa in October 2021. The call received 269 applications of which 192 underwent external scientific review, however, no project was selected for funding because of the transition of the GC Africa programme and termination of Sida support.
